# Volume 5 — CHAPTER XI. A DREADFUL DISCOVERY

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

“Well, you kids have gone and done it now,” Mary said upon meeting them in the Valley. In Hollowmere above, Miss Winifred engaged in an anguished conference alongside Nell and Tabitha, a discussion Mary wished would endure, because a full fortnight had passed since she had last been permitted to make merry with her friends in the beloved rainbow valley.
{: #nw-v05-c11-p0000 }

“Done what?” asked all of them except Edmund, who was lost in his usual reverie.
{: #nw-v05-c11-p0001 }

“I am referring to you youngsters from the manse,” Mary declared. “Your actions were simply terrible. Nothing in the world could have made me do something like that, even though I was not raised in a manse—was not raised anywhere at all—just grew up.”
{: #nw-v05-c11-p0002 }

“What have we done?” Grace asked with a blank expression.
{: #nw-v05-c11-p0003 }

“Finished! Asking would be a wise move! People are saying the most dreadful things. It has likely destroyed your father's standing among these churchgoers. The poor man will certainly never overcome this disgrace! Everyone holds him responsible, which is completely unjust. However, justice does not exist in this life. Each of you should feel deep shame.”
{: #nw-v05-c11-p0004 }

“What have we done?” Ida inquired once more, filled with despair. Grace remained silent, yet her eyes shone with a golden-brown disdain directed at Mary.
{: #nw-v05-c11-p0005 }

“Oh, stop acting like you are innocent,” Mary stated scathingly. “All of us are aware of what you did.”
{: #nw-v05-c11-p0006 }

“I do not,” put in Kit Carrow crossly. “Mary Stubbs, do not let me see you make Ida cry. What is it you are talking about?”
{: #nw-v05-c11-p0007 }

“I guess you are unaware, as you have only recently returned from up west,” Mary said, her tone slightly muted. Kit was continually able to handle her. “However, you can be sure that all the other people are fully aware.”
{: #nw-v05-c11-p0008 }

“Is aware of what?”
{: #nw-v05-c11-p0009 }

“Last Sunday, Grace and Ida didn't go to Sunday School and instead did housecleaning.”
{: #nw-v05-c11-p0010 }

“We didn’t,” Grace and Ida shouted, vehemently denying it.
{: #nw-v05-c11-p0011 }

Mary cast a disdainful glance in their direction.
{: #nw-v05-c11-p0012 }

“Given how you reprimanded me for not telling the truth, I didn’t think you would deny it,” she said. “Why claim you didn’t? It’s common knowledge that you did. Elder Clow and his wife were witnesses. A few folks claim the church will split because of it, though I wouldn’t go to that extreme. You are a fine pair.”
{: #nw-v05-c11-p0013 }

Bess Carrow rose to her feet and wrapped her arms about the bewildered Grace and Ida.
{: #nw-v05-c11-p0014 }

“When you were dying of hunger inside Mr. Taylor’s barn, Mary Stubbs, they had the kindness to welcome you, offer you food, and provide you with clothes,” she remarked. “I have to observe that you show great gratitude.”
{: #nw-v05-c11-p0015 }

“I am thankful,” Mary replied. “You would realize it had you listened to me defending Mr. Ashdown no matter what. My tongue has been blistered from speaking on his behalf this week. Over and over, I have stated that he should not be faulted because his children tidyed up on Sunday. He was not there—and they were well aware.”
{: #nw-v05-c11-p0016 }

“However, we failed to do so,” Ida objected. “The day we tidied the home was Monday. Isn't that right, Grace?”
{: #nw-v05-c11-p0017 }

“Naturally it was,” Grace stated, her eyes flashing. “Despite the rain, we attended Sunday School—and nobody appeared—not even Elder Abraham, regardless of his remarks concerning fair-weather Christians.”
{: #nw-v05-c11-p0018 }

“Saturday brought rain,” Mary stated. “The weather on Sunday turned exceedingly lovely. Toothache kept me from attending Sunday School, though all the others were present and witnessed every bit of your belongings displayed across the lawn. Furthermore, Elder Abraham and Mrs. Elder Abraham observed you beating rugs within the cemetery.”
{: #nw-v05-c11-p0019 }

Taking a seat in the middle of the daisies, Ida started weeping.
{: #nw-v05-c11-p0020 }

“Listen to me,” declared Kit with determination, “we have to get to the bottom of this. A blunder has been made by someone. Grace, Sunday had good weather. What made you think Saturday was Sunday?”
{: #nw-v05-c11-p0021 }

“Prayer-meeting occurred on Thursday night,” Grace exclaimed, “and Adam went into the soup-pot on Friday because he was pursued by Aunt Martha’s cat, which ruined our meal; and a snake was in the cellar on Saturday, but Rupert retrieved it using a forked stick to take it outside, and it rained on Sunday. There now!”
{: #nw-v05-c11-p0022 }

“Prayer-meeting occurred on Wednesday night,” Mary remarked. “Elder Baxter was supposed to lead, but he was unable to make Thursday night, so it got moved to Wednesday. Your count was simply off by one day, Grace Ashdown, and you actually performed labor on Sunday.”
{: #nw-v05-c11-p0023 }

All at once, Grace erupted in a fit of laughing.
{: #nw-v05-c11-p0024 }

“I guess we did. What a laugh!”
{: #nw-v05-c11-p0025 }

“For your father, it’s hardly a joke,” Mary remarked with bitterness.
{: #nw-v05-c11-p0026 }

“Once everyone realizes that it was merely an error, everything will be fine,” Grace remarked casually. “A simple explanation will suffice.”
{: #nw-v05-c11-p0027 }

“You can clarify until you are blue in the gills,” Mary stated, “yet a falsehood of that nature will journey more quickly and wider than you ever could. I HAVE witnessed a greater portion of the world than you, and I am aware. Furthermore, a great deal of people will refuse to accept that it was an accident.”
{: #nw-v05-c11-p0028 }

“They shall should I inform them,” Grace declared.
{: #nw-v05-c11-p0029 }

“You cannot inform everyone,” Mary stated. “No, I am telling you that you have brought shame upon your father.”
{: #nw-v05-c11-p0030 }

Although Ida's night was ruined by this gloomy thought, Grace declined to be distressed. Furthermore, she possessed a scheme that was going to set all things to rights. Consequently, she placed the previous time and its error out of her mind and yielded completely to the pleasure of the current moment. Kit departed in order to angle, while Edmund emerged from his musings and went on to portray the forests of paradise. Mary paid close attention and paid attention with deference. In spite of her dread of Edmund, she delighted in his "book talk." A charming feeling was forever bestowed upon her by it. Edmund's reading of his Coleridge had occurred on that day, and he depicted a paradise in which
{: #nw-v05-c11-p0031 }

“There existed gardens radiant with winding streams where numerous incense-bearing trees produced blossoms, and there existed forests as old as the hills surrounding bright patches of vegetation.”
{: #nw-v05-c11-p0032 }

“I was unaware that heaven contained any woods,” Mary uttered, drawing a deep breath. “My belief was that it consisted entirely of streets—and streets—and streets.”
{: #nw-v05-c11-p0033 }

“Naturally, trees exist there,” Bess remarked. “Since Mother is unable to exist without woods and neither am I, what purpose would entering heaven serve if trees were absent?”
{: #nw-v05-c11-p0034 }

“There are cities, too,” the young dreamer said, “magnificent cities—hued exactly as the sunset, having sapphire towers along with rainbow domes. Gold and diamonds are used to build them—entire streets made of diamonds, glittering such as the sun. Within the squares exist crystal fountains kissed by the light, and the asphodel blooms everywhere—the celestial flower.”
{: #nw-v05-c11-p0035 }

“Fancy!” Mary exclaimed. “After seeing Port Marlow’s main street one time, I considered it truly grand, though I imagine heaven makes it look like nothing. Well, your description makes it all seem magnificent, yet won't it also be rather boring?”
{: #nw-v05-c11-p0036 }

“Oh, I suppose we are able to enjoy ourselves a bit whenever the angels aren't looking,” Grace remarked easily.
{: #nw-v05-c11-p0037 }

“Heaven is all fun,” Izzy declared.
{: #nw-v05-c11-p0038 }

“It is not written in the Bible,” exclaimed Mary, whose extensive Sunday afternoon Bible reading under Miss Winifred’s supervision led her to regard herself as a true expert on the text.
{: #nw-v05-c11-p0039 }

“Mother says the language of the Bible is figurative,” Bess said.
{: #nw-v05-c11-p0040 }

“Is it false, then?” Mary asked with a sense of hope.
{: #nw-v05-c11-p0041 }

“No—not precisely—however my impression is that it signifies heaven will mirror whatever you wish for it to be.”
{: #nw-v05-c11-p0042 }

“I want it to be exactly like Fern Hollow,” Mary remarked, “where I can chatter and mess around with all of you children. I am satisfied with that. Regardless, entering heaven is impossible until our lives end, and even that is uncertain, so why fret over it? Kit has arrived holding a catch of trout, and frying them is now my responsibility.”
{: #nw-v05-c11-p0043 }

“Since we belong to the minister’s family, we should possess a greater knowledge of heaven than Edmund,” remarked Ida, while they made their way back home on that evening.
{: #nw-v05-c11-p0044 }

“We have the exact same knowledge, yet Edmund possesses imagination,” Grace remarked. “According to Mrs. Kerr, this trait comes from his mother.”
{: #nw-v05-c11-p0045 }

“It’s such a shame we got the day wrong regarding Sunday,” Ida said with a sigh.
{: #nw-v05-c11-p0046 }

“Do not be anxious about it. I have devised an excellent scheme for clarifying things so that all will understand,” Grace said. “Only hold off until tomorrow evening.”
{: #nw-v05-c11-p0047 }
